item.title: EU regulators publish draft transparency rules for general-purpose AI models
item.description: The draft rules would require providers of general-purpose models to publish training-data summaries and incident reports. Regulators said the consultation closes on 30 September. Industry groups have asked for a longer comment window.

item.title: Draft EU rules would force AI providers to publish training-data summaries
item.description: Under the draft published this week, providers of general-purpose AI models would file incident reports and publish training-data summaries. The consultation closes on 30 September, regulators said.

item.title: Industry groups push back on EU AI transparency consultation timeline
item.description: Three industry associations said the 30 September deadline gives too little time to respond. A regulator spokesperson said the timeline is not expected to change. The draft does not set penalties yet.

item.title: What the EU's draft general-purpose AI rules would require
item.description: The draft covers training-data summaries, incident reporting and downstream documentation. Regulators said enforcement details will follow in a later text. No penalty schedule has been published.

item.title: Researchers disclose prompt-injection flaw affecting three agent frameworks
item.description: Researchers at Halden University disclosed a prompt-injection technique that bypassed tool-use restrictions in three open-source agent frameworks. Two maintainers shipped patches on Monday. The third has not responded publicly.

item.title: Agent frameworks patched after Halden prompt-injection disclosure
item.description: Two of the three affected agent frameworks released patches on Monday following the Halden University disclosure. Researchers said the technique required no special access to the target system.

item.title: Halden disclosure renews debate over agent tool permissions
item.description: Security engineers said the disclosure shows tool permissions are still granted too broadly by default. One maintainer said the reported technique does not work against the framework's current release.

item.title: Blue Harbor AI reports 10 security findings in Basalt 1 evaluation
item.description: An evaluation released by Blue Harbor AI on Friday lists 10 security findings for Basalt 1. Blue Harbor AI said 2 were resolved before the report went out. No exploit code was published.

item.title: Harbor ai reports 10 security findings in basalt 1 evaluation, Blue Harbor AI says
item.description: Security researchers at Blue Harbor AI said Basalt 1 had 10 findings in their review published Friday. 2 were fixed ahead of disclosure. The severity ratings were assigned by Blue Harbor AI itself.

item.title: What Blue Harbor AI announced: Harbor AI reports 10 security findings in Basalt 1 evaluation
item.description: Blue Harbor AI's Friday report on Basalt 1 describes 10 findings, of which 2 were already patched. A maintainer said the remaining findings require configuration changes rather than code fixes.
